inlines.v: MALIGN, adjective mali'ne. [Latin malignus, from malus, evil. See Malady.] 1. Having a very evil disposition towards others; harboring violent hatred or enmity; malicious; as malign spirits. 2. Unfavorable; pernicious; tending to injure; as a malign aspect of planets. 3. Malignant; pernicious; as a malign ulcer. MALIGN, verb transitive To regard with envy or malice; to treat with extreme enmity; to injure maliciously. The people practice mischief against private men, whom they malign by stealing their goods and murdering them. 1. To traduce; to defame. MALIGN, verb intransitive To entertain malice.
